definitions.explanation: Being in a lower or weaker position relative to others, whether in competition, ability, rank, or negotiating power.

examples.japanese: {劣位|れつい}に{立|た}たされる。
examples.english: To be placed at a disadvantage.

examples.japanese: {技術|ぎじゅつ}{面|めん}で{劣位|れつい}にある。
examples.english: To be in an inferior position technologically.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}で{劣位|れつい}に{立|た}たないよう{準備|じゅんび}する。
examples.english: To prepare so as not to be at a disadvantage in negotiations.

examples.japanese: {市場|しじょう}での{劣位|れつい}を{挽回|ばんかい}するために{新|あたら}しい{戦略|せんりゃく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}した。
examples.english: They launched a new strategy to recover from their inferior market position.

notes:
A formal term describing an inferior or disadvantaged position, often used in business, military, academic, and competitive contexts. Typically contrasted with {優位|ゆうい} (superiority, advantageous position).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {劣位|れつい}に{立|た}つ: to stand in an inferior position
- {劣位|れつい}に{立|た}たされる: to be placed at a disadvantage
- {劣位|れつい}にある: to be in an inferior position
- {劣位|れつい}を{挽回|ばんかい}する: to recover from a disadvantage
- {競争|きょうそう}{劣位|れつい}: competitive disadvantage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {優位|ゆうい}: superiority, advantageous position — the direct opposite
- {劣勢|れっせい}: inferiority, losing position — emphasizes being on the losing side in a contest
- {不利|ふり}: disadvantage — more common in everyday usage
- {下位|かい}: lower rank, lower position — refers to ranking rather than competitive strength

FORMATION:
{劣|れつ} (inferior, worse) + {位|い} (rank, position) — literally "inferior rank."
